title: 2012 AMC 12A Problem 6
statement: The sums of three whole numbers taken in pairs are \(12,\) \(17,\) and \(19.\) What is the middle number?

solutions.text:
Let the numbers be \(a \lt b \lt c.\) Adding the three pairwise sums gives \(2(a+b+c) = 12+17+19\) \(= 48,\) so \(a+b+c = 24.\)

Then \(a = 24-19 = 5,\) \(b = 24-17 = 7,\) and \(c = 24-12 = 12.\) The middle number is \(7.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Adding all three pairwise sums counts each number twice
The total \(a+b+c\) is half of \(12+17+19\); subtract each pair sum to get the third number
